description: The Landslide Exposure Database (LED) is the first building-level national assessment of landslide exposure in the United States, covering 128 million structures in the conterminous states, Alaska and Hawaii. It was produced by Daniel Acosta-Reyes and Joseph Wartman, with data on DesignSafe (2026) and a Zenodo record of 23 March 2026 whose creator is affiliated with the University of Washington. It integrates the USGS landslide susceptibility model, the National Structure Inventory, Overture Maps building footprints and Census Community Resilience Estimates, giving each building a susceptibility class, structural attributes and socioeconomic indicators. The DesignSafe release has LED data by state as GeoPackage and Google Earth KMZ, census tract summaries with an interactive Hazmapper map, map products, and evaluation inventories from Seattle and from Hurricane Helene (2024) in North Carolina; the Zenodo record adds a national building point file of about 9 GB and the processing code. Coverage: the United States. Access: DesignSafe and Zenodo. Licence: Open Data Commons Attribution on DesignSafe and CC BY 4.0 on Zenodo; free. Caveats: a preliminary screening tool, not a substitute for site-specific engineering or geological assessment. Simulation uses: landslide exposure of buildings and vulnerable communities. Related records: the Overture Maps buildings and the USGS HERA exposure data.
